requirements.evidence: Most of the contract is present (Entity/EntityMembership/UserRole, policies, factories, routes/web.php:42-68, lang keys), but two core requirements fail: app/Providers/AppServiceProvider.php:42 registers CurrentEntity as global persistent Livewire middleware, so CurrentEntity.php:29-31 redirects the /livewire/update call of CreateEntity::submit to onboarding for a user with zero memberships and the entity is never created; and database/migrations/2026_10_29_072027_create_entity_memberships_table.php:31-32 runs ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN ... GENERATED ALWAYS AS (...) STORED, which SQLite rejects (only VIRTUAL generated columns can be added by ALTER TABLE), so the required SQLite portability of the one-owner constraint is not met.

conventions.evidence: Good use of #[Validate] (app/Livewire/Entity/CreateEntity.php:19), policies for authorization (app/Policies/EntityPolicy.php:14-50, EntityMembershipPolicy.php:34-49), deliberate $fillable (app/Models/Entity.php:19-22), Blade components (resources/views/livewire/entity/create-entity.blade.php:5), and docs/CHANGELOG updates. Deviation: the entity+owner-membership write is implemented inline in CreateEntity::submit (CreateEntity.php:36-53) instead of an app/Actions/* use case as the conventions require for domain writes.

security.evidence: Server-side authorization is present in every action (CreateEntity.php:26, Dashboard.php:18, routes/web.php:54 abort_unless can('view')), input is validated (CreateEntity.php:19), output is escaped with {{ }} in switcher/dashboard, and fillable is limited. Gap: app/Livewire/Entity/Dashboard.php:14 exposes a public Entity property that is not #[Locked] and is authorized only in mount(), so a re-hydrated/tampered model key would not re-run the policy; impact is limited because the component has no write actions.

tests.evidence: Substantial coverage across EntityTest, EntityMembershipTest, EntityPoliciesTest, EntityOnboardingTest and EntityTenantSessionTest (DB constraints, slug retry, audit log, policy matrix, 403s, switcher markup, navbar link). Missing: the conventions' mandated unauthorized-call and tamper tests for CreateEntity::submit (tests/Feature/EntityOnboardingTest.php only tests the page redirect and happy paths), and no HTTP-level test exercises the persistent middleware on an update request, which is why the onboarding blocker is not caught.

simplicity.evidence: Lean relations/scopes/policies, no speculative abstractions, reuses the existing layouts/components. Minor duplication: the 0/1/many dispatch is written twice (routes/web.php:24-39 and app/Http/Middleware/CurrentEntity.php:26-39), which can drift.

readability.evidence: Small focused methods, clear naming (uniqueSlug, membershipFor, roleFor, isManager), useful PHPDoc/comments and no dead code or debug output; the retry loop (CreateEntity.php:29-58) is easy to follow.

scope.evidence: The entity work is scoped correctly, but the diff also adds two unrelated CI/deploy pipelines (.github/workflows/deploy-dev.yml:1, .github/workflows/tests.yml:1) and an unrelated no-op middleware array edit (routes/web.php:92).

issues.explanation: Registering CurrentEntity as global persistent Livewire middleware runs it on every /livewire/update request; for a user with zero memberships it redirects CreateEntity::submit to onboarding before the action runs, so the first entity can never be created in the browser, and the Livewire::test suite bypasses this middleware so it does not catch it.

SQLite does not allow adding a STORED generated column with ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN (only VIRTUAL is permitted), so this migration fails on SQLite and the explicitly required SQLite/MariaDB portability of the owner_seq constraint is broken; define the column inside Schema::create (or use storedAs) instead.
These new deploy/CI pipelines (deploy to a VPS, run bin/pf up/smoke, workflow secrets) are unrelated to the entities onboarding task and were not requested.

Creating the entity and its owner membership is a domain write but is implemented inline in the Livewire component instead of an app/Actions/* class, contrary to the project's "domain writes go through Actions" convention.
The public Entity property is neither #[Locked] nor authorized outside mount(), so authorization is not re-applied if the serialized model key is altered on a later update request.
There is no unauthorized-call or tamper test for CreateEntity::submit (and no HTTP-level update test), although the conventions require both for every Livewire action.

A user whose only membership belongs to a soft-deleted entity resolves entity to null and gets a URL-generation error from redirect()->route('entity.dashboard', null), while CurrentEntity.php:41-44 aborts 403 instead of treating that case as "no membership" (onboarding); the switcher can similarly become empty for multiple soft-deleted memberships.

The contract asks for a unique slug, but the factory only makes the name unique and derives the slug from it, so two distinct names that slugify identically would violate entities_slug_unique and flake tests.
Changing middleware('throttle:6,1') to middleware(['throttle:6,1']) is a behaviour-neutral edit unrelated to the task.
The onboarding/switcher/dashboard dispatch rules are duplicated in the /home closure and the middleware, so a change to one can silently diverge from the other.

review.summary: The change implements the entity/membership model, policies, tenant session, onboarding, switcher, dashboard and navbar entry, with extensive tests and updated docs, largely matching the contract. It is not mergeable as-is: the globally persisted CurrentEntity middleware blocks the first-entity onboarding submit over HTTP, and the raw STORED generated-column ALTER breaks the required SQLite portability; it also adds unrelated CI/deploy workflows and bypasses the Actions convention for the entity write.
